Raise anticipated witness objections outside the jury’s presence in advance; bench conferences are kept to a minimum.

docs.t: Judge Suzanne Mitchell (W.D. Okla.) — Experts, instructions, and privacy
docs.x: Judge Suzanne Mitchell, W.D. Okla.. Experts, instructions, and privacy: Do not ask the court to certify a witness as an expert. Give as much advance notice as possible of difficult legal or evidentiary questions. In closing, you may preview what the court’s instruction will say but may not read or quote any instruction. Avoid eliciting restricted personal data (full Social Security or account numbers, minors’ names, full birth dates, and in criminal cases home addresses beyond city and state); if mentioned, you may ask to strike or redact it.

docs.t: Judge Suzanne Mitchell (W.D. Okla.) — Proposed orders and contact
docs.x: Judge Suzanne Mitchell, W.D. Okla.. Proposed orders and contact: Send proposed orders to mitchell-orders@okwd.uscourts.gov. Chambers: Room 4001, Courtroom 401 (fourth floor), Oklahoma City; phone 405-609-5220; courtroom deputy (Adam) 405-609-5044.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Filing and citing exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Filing and citing exhibits (trap): File the motion and exhibits before the supporting brief so the brief can cite their docket numbers; exhibits may be attached to the motion or filed separately after it. For a response or reply, first file an appendix of exhibits. Give each exhibit a number and descriptive identifier (for example, “Exh. 1 – Smith Dep.”). Cite docket number, attachment number, and PDF header page, as in (Dkt. 42-8 at 5); for depositions add page and line, as in (Dkt. 32-1 at 16 (Smith Dep. at 16:7-9)). When relying on a deposition excerpt, include the cited pages and at least the three pages immediately before and after.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Summary judgment (trap): Before moving, contact all other counsel to learn whether anyone else plans to move. If cross-motions are planned, use the judge’s four-brief schedule: Party A’s motion and brief (35 pages); Party B’s cross-motion, brief, and response (55 pages); Party A’s reply and response (40 pages); Party B’s reply (20 pages). A different process requires a motion stating all counsel’s positions. Motions to exceed page limits and collateral motions such as motions to strike are disfavored. Cite specific evidence for each fact in both the fact and argument sections, or the fact may be disregarded.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Other motions
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Other motions: When a complaint is amended as of course after a Rule 12 motion, the judge’s standard practice is to deny the Rule 12 motion without prejudice as moot. TRO and preliminary injunction motions must address each Rule 65 requirement and also when the irreparable harm will occur, whether discovery is needed, whether an evidentiary or argument hearing is sought, and a proposed timeline.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Oral argument: The parties should confer and file a joint motion requesting oral argument with the pertinent motion. A party may file a Request for Oral Argument for Less Experienced Attorney (an attorney practicing less than 7 years) while a motion is being briefed or promptly after, stating that a Less Experienced Attorney will argue the motion or a significant portion of it. This applies to all motions in full-consent cases and motions referred in non-consent cases. The court will grant the request and hold argument if at all practicable (still discretionary), and more experienced co-counsel may assist during argument only as appropriate. All attorneys must be fully prepared on the record and the law; the court draws no inference from a party’s choice whether to use a Less Experienced Attorney.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Final pretrial conference: About four weeks before the conference, the court issues an order setting filing deadlines; if they differ from the CMP, the order controls. Meet and confer beforehand on the final pretrial order, and bring copies of proposed exhibits. File motions in limine as one document, numbering each issue; the opponent responds to each with “no objection” or “objection” plus argument.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Jury selection and trial day
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Jury selection and trial day: Questionnaires are available the business day (usually Friday) before trial; refer to jurors only by number. The court questions the whole panel and provides its proposed questions before the final pretrial conference; counsel may get brief follow-up. Each side has at least 3 peremptory challenges in civil cases. The court ordinarily seats 8 jurors (typically no fewer than 7), with no alternates. Be in the courtroom by 8:00 a.m. on the first day; the jury typically comes in at 9:00 a.m. and leaves around 5:00 p.m. If both sides will call a witness, all questioning usually occurs in plaintiff’s case.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Depositions at trial (trap): Mark portions to be read on the original transcript and offer it as an exhibit (it does not go to the jury); a person in the witness box reads the answers. Deposition summaries are acceptable only by stipulation. Deposed treating medical providers are presumed “unavailable” under Fed. R. Civ. P. 32(a)(4); a written objection must be filed at least 30 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Exhibits and stipulations
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Exhibits and stipulations: Number exhibits only, using one system from the start of discovery. Move stipulated exhibits in at the start of trial; offer others when they become admissible. Prepare three exhibit binders for the court. Show demonstratives to opposing counsel before trial and object at the first opportunity; only unopposed demonstratives may be shown without leave. In bench trials, only exhibits mentioned at trial are considered admitted unless stipulated otherwise. Arrange oversized exhibits at least two weeks, and a court VEPS at least three weeks, before trial. Bring a wifi hot spot if needed.

docs.t: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman (S.D. Ind.) — Openings, closings, and courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge Crystal S. Wildeman, S.D. Ind.. Openings, closings, and courtroom conduct: Opening time is set at the final pretrial conference and closing time at trial. Plaintiff must state any suggested damages number in the opening segment of closing. The court ordinarily reads final instructions after closings; proposed instructions must cite authority. Only the attorney handling a witness’s direct may object during that witness’s cross, and vice versa. Phones must be silent; in session they may be used only to text about witnesses and logistics. Courtroom deputy Tricia Blanford, 812-434-6420.

docs.t: Judge Kellie M. Barr (S.D. Ind.) — Oral argument for less experienced attorneys
docs.x: Judge Kellie M. Barr, S.D. Ind.. Oral argument for less experienced attorneys: A party may file a Request for Oral Argument for Less Experienced Attorney (an attorney practicing less than 7 years) while a motion is being briefed or promptly after, stating that a Less Experienced Attorney will argue the motion or a significant portion of it. This applies to all motions in full-consent cases and motions referred in non-consent cases. The court will grant the request and hold argument if at all practicable (still discretionary), and more experienced co-counsel may assist during argument only as appropriate. All attorneys must be fully prepared on the record and the law; the court draws no inference from a party’s choice whether to use a Less Experienced Attorney.

docs.t: Judge Kellie M. Barr (S.D. Ind.) — Protective orders
docs.x: Judge Kellie M. Barr, S.D. Ind.. Protective orders: The page links the court’s Uniform Stipulated Protective Order (updated April 18, 2022), which the court calls presumptively acceptable. It does not authorize sealing; follow S.D. Ind. L.R. 5-11.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Agreed protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Agreed protective orders (trap): File a motion attaching the proposed order. Use the court’s Uniform Protective Order or explain in the motion why a different form is proposed; if you use the uniform form, the motion must identify every change made to it. Replace Section VIII of the uniform form (or include in any alternative form) the judge’s required sealing language, or explain any deviation in detail: comply with L.R. 5-11, over-redaction may lead to denial of a motion to seal, and before moving to challenge a “Confidential” or “Attorneys’ Eyes Only” designation, the parties must request a telephonic conference with the magistrate judge. Any order allowing “Attorneys’ Eyes Only” designations must precisely define what may be so designated. File the motion as soon as practicable, and no later than 14 days before the original due date of any discovery

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Trial day and promptness
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Trial day and promptness: Trial usually runs 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with a one-hour lunch at noon and short breaks. Be in the courtroom at least 15 minutes before each day’s start; the courtroom opens by 8:00 a.m. Have the next witness ready when court resumes. If there is a substantial delay between witnesses, the court may deem that you have rested.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Jury selection: The venire list and questionnaires are available at least one day before trial and must be picked up in person (no email or fax); return all copies once the jury is chosen. Submit proposed voir dire questions as the scheduling order requires; the court conducts most of voir dire, and counsel may have brief follow-up from the lectern, without argument or asking about verdict amounts. Each side gets at least 3 peremptory challenges, exercised simultaneously and in writing. The court ordinarily seats 8 jurors with no alternates; all deliberate.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Openings, closings, and examination
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Openings, closings, and examination: Raise in advance with the court and opposing counsel any unstipulated exhibit or display for opening, or any display not in evidence for closing, or it may be barred. “Two minutes remain” means time has expired. Plaintiff must state any suggested damages number in the opening segment of closing, and spend most closing time there. Examine from the lectern; avoid listed improper question forms (for example, “Is it fair to say?” or negative questions). The court may allow written juror questions. Stand to object and state grounds briefly. Only the attorney handling a witness’s direct may object during that witness’s cross, and vice versa.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Depositions at trial (trap): Mark portions to be read on the original transcript and offer it as an exhibit (it does not go to the jury); for video, offer both video and marked transcript. A person in the witness box reads the answers. Treating physicians and other health care providers who have been deposed are presumed “unavailable” under Fed. R. Civ. P. 32(a)(4). A written objection showing good cause must be filed at least 45 days before trial. Deposition summaries are encouraged but must be stipulated or provided to opposing counsel before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Exhibits
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Exhibits: Number exhibits only (not “Plaintiff’s Exhibit 1”), using one numbering system from the start of discovery that carries through depositions and trial. Prepare copies for each juror, the witness, opposing counsel, and two for the court (usually 13 in civil trials); tabbed juror notebooks are strongly urged. Counsel must bring their own exhibit labels. Number each page of each exhibit. Even stipulated exhibits must be offered on the record to be admitted. Arrange oversized exhibits or models with the courtroom deputy at least two weeks before trial, and a Video Evidence Presentation System at least three weeks before trial.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Instructions, pretrial conference, and transcripts
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Instructions, pretrial conference, and transcripts: File proposed jury instructions per the pretrial orders, each citing authority; the deputy can provide recent instructions. Instructions usually precede closing arguments, and jurors get copies. Bring one copy of proposed exhibits to the final pretrial conference, which covers witnesses, exhibits, settlement, stipulations, deposition objections, instructions, timing, and motions in limine. Arrange daily transcripts with the court reporter at least two weeks before trial, and give the reporter a list of unusual terms and names.

docs.t: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore (S.D. Ind.) — Courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge Mark J. Dinsmore, S.D. Ind.. Courtroom conduct: Stand when speaking and use the lectern; address remarks to the court, not opposing counsel. No approval needed to approach a witness with an exhibit. Cell phones must be turned off (not silent) in the courtroom; only bottled water is allowed. Courtroom deputy Geeta DeVellen, (317) 229-3908, answers questions on trial procedures.

docs.t: Judge Tim A. Baker (S.D. Ind.) — Trial day and promptness
docs.x: Judge Tim A. Baker, S.D. Ind.. Trial day and promptness: Trial usually runs 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with a one-hour lunch at noon and short breaks. Be in the courtroom at least 15 minutes before each day’s start; it opens at least 30 minutes before proceedings. Have the next witness ready when court resumes. If there is a substantial delay between witnesses, the court may deem that you have rested.

docs.t: Judge Tim A. Baker (S.D. Ind.) — Exhibits and presentation (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tim A. Baker, S.D. Ind.. Exhibits and presentation (trap): Counsel are expected to know and use the court’s Video Evidence Presentation System (VEPS) to display exhibits; if it is unavailable, juror notebooks may be required. Contact the courtroom deputy at least one week before the final pretrial conference about equipment and training. Mark exhibits before trial, by number only, using one numbering system agreed from the start of discovery; counsel must supply labels for any exhibit marked in court. Disclose oversized exhibits or models no later than the final pretrial conference. Raise in advance any unstipulated exhibit for opening or any display not in evidence for closing, or it may be barred.

docs.t: Judge Tim A. Baker (S.D. Ind.) — Depositions and stipulations
docs.x: Judge Tim A. Baker, S.D. Ind.. Depositions and stipulations: Stipulations on exhibit admissibility, authenticity, and facts are expected. Edit deposition designations (including video) with opposing counsel; deposition summaries are acceptable only by stipulation.

docs.t: Judge Tim A. Baker (S.D. Ind.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge Tim A. Baker, S.D. Ind.. Jury selection: The venire list and questionnaires are available at least one day before trial; return them once the jury is chosen. Submit proposed voir dire questions per the scheduling order; the court conducts most of voir dire, with brief follow-up by counsel from the lectern. Jurors may take notes.

docs.t: Judge Tim A. Baker (S.D. Ind.) — Courtroom conduct and transcripts
docs.x: Judge Tim A. Baker, S.D. Ind.. Courtroom conduct and transcripts: Stand when speaking and use the lectern; address the court, not opposing counsel. No permission needed to approach a witness with an exhibit. Cell phones off in court; only bottled water allowed. Arrange real-time or daily transcripts with the court reporter at least two weeks before trial. Courtroom deputy Denise Brown, (317) 229-3707, answers trial-procedure questions.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Hearings and rescheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Hearings and rescheduling (trap): Judge Stinnett prefers to hold criminal and civil court on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, usually in Courtroom C on the fourth floor in Lexington. Civil cases: you must file a motion to move a hearing date or time, and the judge prefers that the parties first confer and agree on a new date and time. Criminal cases: file a motion, but in limited, exigent circumstances the judge accepts scheduling requests by email or phone if counsel confirms opposing counsel was contacted first. Judge Stinnett cannot change any district judge’s hearing or trial calendar.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Discovery disputes: call first, motion later (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Discovery disputes: call first, motion later (trap): Unless the judge orders otherwise in represented cases, disputes follow the district judge’s scheduling order and a call process: first make the good-faith effort LR 37.1 requires; the court proceeds only after you comply and tell it so. Then email Stinnett_Chambers@kyed.uscourts.gov, copying all counsel, with a 2–3 sentence summary, confirmation of LR 37.1 compliance, the urgency, the parties needed, the expected length of the call, and dates all necessary counsel are available. The judge enters an order setting a conference call. After the call, the judge quickly issues a succinct, provisional ruling; either side may then file a fully briefed formal motion (mindful of LR 37.1), and the resulting opinion is appealable to the district judge.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Discovery Dispute Worksheet (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Discovery Dispute Worksheet (trap): Before the call, as the scheduling order directs, each party emails a completed Civil Discovery Dispute Worksheet (party, case, attorneys on the call, factual summary, procedural posture, LR 37.1 and FRCP 37 efforts, and facts and legal arguments), copying opposing counsel. The party that served a written request, deposition notice, or subpoena in dispute must attach only the portions of the request and response at issue; strictly targeted portions of other papers may also be attached. Failing to complete the worksheet or attach the underlying discovery may mean a ruling against you or denial of relief.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Case management
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Case management: Judge Stinnett manages scheduling, discovery, and pretrial motions in Judge Boom’s and Judge Wier’s civil cases, consent cases, and assigned habeas and pro se cases, and handles discovery disputes in all civil cases assigned to the judge; district judges also refer specific motions case by case. In cases where the judge manages discovery (other than pro se cases), expect a status teleconference with counsel before discovery closes to check on deadlines.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Settlement conferences (trap): Request a settlement conference jointly, by formal motion or email to chambers. Exceptions: Judge Reeves’s scheduling order bars a magistrate-judge settlement conference without Judge Reeves’s prior approval, and in a case before Judge Stinnett by consent, send the request to Magistrate Judge Atkins. Negotiate in good faith before submitting the written conference summary. All parties and representatives attend in person unless they get specific permission at least one week before; counsel arranges the technology for anyone appearing by video. The parties may ask (through chambers or by motion) to hold the whole conference by Microsoft Teams, with a joint room and private breakout rooms.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Protective orders and sealing
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Protective orders and sealing: The judge will approve agreed protective orders, confidentiality agreements, and motions to seal consistent with case law and the Local Rules. Central Division standing order (June 1, 2020): all warrants in magistrate matters, with applications, affidavits, and attachments, are sealed until returned. After return, the United States has fourteen (14) days to move to keep them sealed; otherwise they, and the returns, are unsealed automatically unless the court orders otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Consent to magistrate judge
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Consent to magistrate judge: Judge Stinnett encourages consent to preside over the whole case, including dispositive motions and trial, and says secure trial dates can generally be accommodated because the judge does not handle felony criminal cases. Use the posted AO 85 consent form.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Contacting chambers: Counsel may email (Stinnett_Chambers@kyed.uscourts.gov) or call ((859) 300-8120) chambers about scheduling or administrative matters; pro se parties may communicate only by email. Filing and CM/ECF questions go to the Clerk’s Office or the CM/ECF Help Desk ((866) 485-6349).

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Criminal and petty offense matters
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Criminal and petty offense matters: Notify the Central Division magistrate judges of all new arrests or entries into federal custody through the court’s New Arrest Notification Portal, which prompts the court to set a hearing. Petty offense (violation notice) docket call: third Thursday of February, April, June, August, October, and December at 1:00 p.m.; arrive by 12:30 p.m. to speak with the prosecutor or contest a violation. Unsealed executed search warrants and other magistrate matters are available on CM/ECF.

docs.t: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett (E.D. Ky.) — Recordings and transcripts
docs.x: Judge Matthew A. Stinnett, E.D. Ky.. Recordings and transcripts: Hearings are generally recorded by Electronic Court Reporting. To get the audio, file the audio-recording order form in the case; for a certified transcript, file the transcript form in the case and the court reporter will contact you. Questions: (859) 514-2252.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial order (trap): Use the judge’s form of proposed pretrial order and email the joint proposed order to CDLIntake_OKND@oknd.uscourts.gov. The form requires, among other things, a particularized statement of damages and other relief for each claim and a summary of each witness’s testimony, noting any witness presented by video. Exchange all trial exhibits early enough to list objections and responses in the proposed order and to meet and confer on them first. List exhibits by Bates number or other distinct identifier; broad categories such as “medical records” are impermissible. Exhibits and witnesses not in the final pretrial order are excluded absent a written motion showing good cause and manifest injustice.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Motions in limine and Daubert (trap): File them by the Scheduling Order deadline; any filed after the pretrial conference will not be considered absent manifest injustice. Absent leave, present all limine issues in a single motion and brief, and submit a copy of the evidence sought to be excluded with the briefing.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Exhibit notebooks and pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Exhibit notebooks and pretrial conference: Prepare exhibit notebooks for the witness stand, opposing party, the judge, and the judge’s law clerk. The judge’s set goes to the courtroom deputy at least three days before the pretrial conference; the rest must be ready the morning of trial. The same rule applies to evidentiary hearings (three days before the hearing). At the pretrial conference, be ready to argue pending motions, exhibit objections, and requested voir dire and instructions, and to raise anything that would otherwise need bench conferences at trial.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Before trial
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Before trial: Email a joint statement of the case (to be read to the venire) to the judge’s intake box at least three days before trial. Be in the courtroom, ready, 30 minutes before the jury-trial start time on day one. Give opposing counsel any Fed. R. Evid. 1006 summary or 107 illustrative aid 14 days before trial; motions to exclude are due 7 days before trial. Pre-mark exhibits per the pretrial order; court time may not be used for marking. Daily copy requires advance permission and arrangement with the court reporter. Give the court and reporter a glossary of technical or unusual terms before trial.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Voir dire: The judge questions the venire and may use the parties’ proposed questions. Supplemental attorney questioning, if allowed, is limited to 20 minutes per party, with no argument, questions about anticipated evidence or law, or commitment hypotheticals.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Witnesses and examination
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Witnesses and examination: Have enough witnesses for a full day; at the end of each day, tell the court and opposing counsel the next day’s witnesses and order. Edit video testimony before trial to conform to rulings. Examine from the lectern: direct, cross, one redirect, and one recross absent exceptional circumstances. Only the attorney handling the witness may raise or respond to objections. Courtroom demonstrations require advance permission outside the jury’s presence.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Jury instructions: File requested instructions and verdict forms per the Scheduling Order and email a Word copy to the intake box; each instruction must cite a model instruction or authority. Objections and case law are due at least five days before trial. The judge holds an informal off-record conference, then an on-record one, and reads final instructions before closings.

docs.t: Judge Christine D Little (N.D. Okla.) — Conduct before the jury
docs.x: Judge Christine D Little, N.D. Okla.. Conduct before the jury: Openings and closings from the lectern; keep objections short, and make no motions (for example, mistrial or judgment as a matter of law) in the jury’s presence. Do not ask the judge to declare a witness an expert. The page also links the court-wide Protective Orders page: a motion for a discovery protective order must state the factual basis and all parties’ positions, attach the CV-29 (confidential) or CV-29a (highly confidential) template customized in redline or track changes, explain every change (or state none was made), and certify compliance with these instructions.

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial order (trap): Use the judge’s form, with a single joint statement of the case (separate statements not allowed) and specific issues of fact and law. Exhibit lists (joint list allowed, otherwise one per party) must omit impeachment or rebuttal items, expert CVs and reports, depositions, demonstratives, and pleadings. Use two columns: each exhibit listed separately in offering order, and any objection with the Federal Rule it rests on. Furnish all exhibits to opposing counsel before the pretrial conference. List primary witnesses and secondary (reserve) witnesses separately, each with a concise statement of testimony; testimony on other subjects and unlisted witnesses are not allowed absent court order.

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Deposition designations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Deposition designations (trap): File designations and counter-designations as a pleading listing witness, page, line, and basis for objection (not the transcript). Submit hard-copy transcripts, highlighted in different colors with objections in the margins, to the Court Clerk per the scheduling order (not filed). Objections are considered only after a personal meeting between counsel; then file unresolved objections separately with a table of page, line, and basis. The same reader reads a witness’s testimony throughout, absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Motions in limine: File one omnibus motion in limine addressing every issue; counsel may seek relief from the usual page limit.

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Voir dire and openings
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Voir dire and openings: Attorney voir dire, if approved before trial, is limited to 15 minutes per side, solely to learn about jurors: no previewing evidence or law, explaining the burden of proof, hypotheticals, or seeking commitments. Openings are limited to 20 minutes per side unless the case is unusually complex, and may be reduced per party in multi-party cases.

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Exhibits and juror notebooks
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Exhibits and juror notebooks: Mark exhibits before court; tell opposing counsel which exhibits will be used before each day’s session. Unobjected exhibits that will certainly be used must be pre-admitted before trial. Pass exhibits to the jury sparingly; ideally have a copy for each juror. In complex cases, identical juror notebooks are allowed after counsel confer on contents (for example, preliminary instructions, admitted exhibits, stipulations, and agreed glossaries or timelines).

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Witnesses and examination
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Witnesses and examination: Direct, cross, one redirect, and one recross except in exceptional circumstances. Do not greet adverse witnesses; address witnesses by surname (except children). Only the attorney handling the witness raises or responds to objections. Rule on videotaped testimony objections early enough to edit the video before it is shown.

docs.t: Judge Jodi F Jayne (N.D. Okla.) — Courtroom protocol
docs.x: Judge Jodi F Jayne, N.D. Okla.. Courtroom protocol: Follow Local General Rule 3. Do not leave the courtroom during trial without leave; clear computer use with the courtroom deputy before the morning of trial. No food, gum, or beverages other than bottled water. Keep objections short; no arguing objections or rulings, and no motions, in the jury’s presence. Do not ask the court to declare a witness an expert. Give advance notice of difficult legal or evidentiary questions in a trial brief or at the pretrial conference. The page also links the court-wide Protective Orders page: a motion for a discovery protective order must state the factual basis and all parties’ positions, attach the CV-29 (confidential) or CV-29a (highly confidential) template customized in redline or track changes, explain every change (or state none was made), and certify compliance with these instructions.

docs.t: Judge Mark T Steele (N.D. Okla.) — Joint discovery status reports
docs.x: Judge Mark T Steele, N.D. Okla.. Joint discovery status reports: When ordered, file a Joint Discovery Status Report every 30 days after the Scheduling Order, listing dates written discovery was served and answered, volume of documents produced, depositions taken and remaining, subpoenas issued and documents obtained, and any discovery issues for the court.

docs.t: Judge Mark T Steele (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial order (trap)

docs.t: Judge Mark T Steele (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Mark T Steele, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial conference: Follow LCvR 16-1 and exchange all proposed exhibits before the conference. Be ready to argue exhibit objections, pending dispositive motions, and motions in limine; the court intends to finish the conference with the case trial-ready.

docs.t: Judge Mark T Steele (N.D. Okla.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark T Steele, N.D. Okla.. Trial (trap): Attorney-conducted voir dire is allowed, subject to time limits. Prepare separate exhibit notebooks for the witness stand, opposing counsel, the court, and the courtroom deputy. Examine from the lectern and do not approach a witness without permission. No speaking objections; bench conferences are discouraged. Examination is limited to direct, cross, one redirect, and one recross. Address witnesses by last name. Finish all video editing before trial. At the end of each trial day, tell the court and opposing counsel the next day’s witnesses and order.

docs.x: Judge Mark T Steele, N.D. Okla.. docs.x: Judge Susan E Huntsman, N.D. Okla.. docs.x: Judge Susan E Huntsman, N.D. Okla.. docs.t: Judge Anita M. Boor (W.D. Wis.) — Deposition disputes
docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Deposition disputes: Judge Boor will hold same-day telephonic hearings on disputes during depositions whenever possible. First make one last good-faith effort and agree on what the dispute is, then call the clerk’s office (608-264-5156) with the case name and number, the attorneys calling, the witness and the witness’s relationship to the case, and a brief description of the dispute. The clerk sets the hearing at the soonest available time, on the call or by ECF notice with dial-in details; do not expect an immediate transfer. Keep using the time (for example, depose around the disputed issue). The hearing is audio recorded, or the deposition reporter may transcribe it; notify the court immediately if the dispute resolves.

docs.t: Judge Anita M. Boor (W.D. Wis.) — Summary judgment: proposed findings of fact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Summary judgment: proposed findings of fact (trap): A motion must include the motion, a statement of proposed findings of fact containing every fact needed to sustain it (including jurisdiction and party identity), supporting evidence, and a brief. The court will not consider facts that appear only in a brief and will not search the record. Each fact goes in a separate numbered paragraph limited to a single proposition, without argument, followed by a record citation (docket number where possible; give the date when a witness has multiple affidavits or depositions). Put a key document (contract, patent, policy) into the record with a single proposed fact; do not restate its provisions or argue its meaning. docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Summary judgment: responses, replies, and sur-replies (trap): The opponent must respond to every proposed fact in separate paragraphs with the same numbers, repeating each fact verbatim, stating disputed or undisputed, and citing contrary evidence; a fact is deemed undisputed unless properly disputed. New facts belong in the opponent’s own additional proposed findings, not in responses, and the court disregards non-responsive facts. Overly argumentative responses or replies may be struck. The reply must repeat verbatim the full sequence (fact, response, reply) so it is a self-contained history, and the movant responds to any additional proposed facts at the same time. The court encourages exchanging Word versions of fact statements. No sur-reply without permission, granted only in rare, unusual situations. Pro se litigants are held to the same procedures,

docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Do not duplicate the court’s standard voir dire questions and instructions, which are attached and generally used in every case. By the response deadline: responses to motions in limine, exhibit objections, deposition objections and counter-designations, and responses to the other side’s voir dire, verdict forms, and instructions. Plaintiff’s counsel convenes the conference and files the Joint Pretrial Statement (defense counsel does so if plaintiff is pro se); failure to cooperate is sanctionable. By the first deadline each side also files numbered proposed findings of fact (marking stipulated facts), a proposed special verdict as if the case were tried to a jury, motions in limine including Daubert motions (unless set earlier), and short explanations of contested legal issues and deposition disputes; trial briefs are optional. docs.t: Judge Anita M. Boor (W.D. Wis.) — Exhibits and electronic evidence
docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Exhibits and electronic evidence: Do not docket trial exhibits. List exhibits on the court’s form with exhibit number, sponsoring witness, and description; plaintiff generally uses 1–500 and defendant 501 and up. Object by filing a new copy of the opponent’s exhibit list with the objection column completed. Unless otherwise directed, submit electronic copies of trial exhibits by 4:00 p.m. on the business day before trial. Under court-wide Administrative Order 434, use Box for Federal Government (preferred) or a flash drive, allowed file formats only (no zip files), 1 GB per file maximum, named “Case Number_Party Role_Party Name_Exhibit Number.” Each side keeps custody of its exhibits and arranges their inclusion in any appeal record; an exhibit referred to at trial becomes part of the record.

docs.t: Judge Anita M. Boor (W.D. Wis.) — Witnesses, fees, and closing the case
docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Witnesses, fees, and closing the case: Motions for writs of habeas corpus ad testificandum for incarcerated witnesses, and requests for subpoenas for unwilling witnesses, are due four weeks before trial with the supporting affidavits the procedures describe; subpoenas should reach the Marshal at least two weeks before trial, with witness fee and mileage tendered for non-incarcerated witnesses. Fee requests must state the legal basis and include contemporaneous task-level time logs, hourly rates, and affidavits on billing judgment and market rates (a billing attorney’s “usual” rate is typically insufficient); opponents must object with particularity. The court will not take a case off the trial calendar for an informal settlement; file a stipulation or joint motion. docs.t: Judge Anita M. Boor (W.D. Wis.) — Criminal final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Anita M. Boor, W.D. Wis.. Criminal final pretrial conference: The telephonic final pretrial conference finalizes voir dire and jury instructions from the court’s circulated drafts; by the submission deadline, propose each edit, deletion, or addition in a separate numbered paragraph citing the draft question or page. Defendants are encouraged to share theory-of-defense instructions or submit them ex parte for in camera review. All motions in limine are due by the submission deadline and must be raised at the conference. The government must file notice of intent to offer prior felony convictions, Rule 404(b) evidence, Rule 801(d)(2)(C)–(E) statements, and Rule 804–807 evidence by then, and must give notice of audio or video recordings (with transcripts) two weeks before the conference; defendants respond one week before. Witness and exhibit lists are submitted ex parte and under seal

docs.x: Judge Ethan A. Hougah, D.N.J.. docs.x: Judge Ethan A. Hougah, D.N.J.. Adjournments and extensions (trap): Request by letter on CM/ECF after seeking all parties’ consent. State the date of the conference or deadline, the length requested, the basis, whether all parties consent or oppose, and whether granting it would affect other dates. docs.x: Judge Ethan A. Hougah, D.N.J.. Courtesy copies: Mail or courier one courtesy copy to chambers of any submission over 30 pages and of any submission filed under seal.

Use the Appendix S form discovery confidentiality order if possible; if the parties propose their own, submit a clean, signature-ready version and a redline showing how it differs from Appendix S. A confidentiality order does not itself authorize filing under seal.

docs.x: Judge Ethan A. Hougah, D.N.J.. Arrange in advance for any other needed participant, such as an insurer representative. Disclose confidentially, no later than 5 business days before the conference, any legal, institutional, insurance-related, or other limit on settlement authority, describing the approval process and who may need to participate. No later than 5 business days before, email a confidential memorandum of no more than 5 double-spaced pages to njdnef_hougah@njd.uscourts.gov (case name, civil action number, conference date, and purpose in the subject line; not filed or served). docs.t: Judge Ethan A. Hougah (D.N.J.) — Final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Ethan A. Hougah, D.N.J.. Final pretrial conference: Trial counsel and a knowledgeable party representative with full settlement authority attend unless permission was granted to participate by telephone; the court may order settlement memoranda in advance. The conference proceeds despite pending dispositive motions unless otherwise ordered. Use the court’s Uniform Final Pretrial Order. Unless otherwise directed, email the joint proposed final pretrial order to njdnef_hougah@njd.uscourts.gov no later than 21 days before the conference and mail one courtesy copy to chambers.

docs.x: Judge Ethan A. Hougah, D.N.J.. Pro hac vice and accuracy of filings: Pro hac vice applications are by formal motion under Local Civil Rule 101.1(c), stating whether all parties consent. Late or over-length submissions, or those with clearly erroneous statements or citations to purported legal authority, may not be considered and may draw sanctions.

docs.x: Judge David T. Schultz, D. Minn.. Courtesy copies: Courtesy copies of motion-related papers are not required. Otherwise, the Practice Pointers refer counsel to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Local Rules.

docs.x: Judge John F. Docherty, D. Minn.. Informal dispute resolution (IDR) (trap): IDR is available for non-dispositive disputes only if all parties agree; otherwise the dispute must be brought by formal motion. There is usually no briefing and no declarations or affidavits. Each party submits a letter of no more than three single-spaced pages, with no exhibits. Only one issue per party unless other arrangements are made at least one week before the IDR call. Two business days after the letters, a Zoom audio-only call is held and the judge rules orally at its end, with no written order or report and recommendation, so an IDR ruling cannot be appealed to the district judge or the Eighth Circuit.

Even if the parties agree to submit a motion on the papers, contact chambers to set a submission date; the matter is deemed submitted on receipt of the last filing, and the court decides whether to hold a hearing. Rescheduling requests must come jointly. Hearings may be by Zoom only if all parties agree; if any party objects, the hearing is in person, so confer on preferences before contacting chambers.

docs.t: Judge John F. Docherty (D. Minn.) — Meet and confer and motion practice
docs.x: Judge John F. Docherty, D. Minn.. If a pending motion is resolved in whole or in part, notify chambers as soon as possible (by joint stipulation under Local Rule 7.1 if time permits) so the hearing can be removed or narrowed. No paper courtesy copies; the judge prefers not to receive hard copies.

docs.t: Judge John F. Docherty (D. Minn.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge John F. Docherty, D. Minn.. Hearings: Cite the record by CM/ECF docket number (for example, “Dkt. No. 22,” not “Exhibit M”). Bring hard copies of any visual aids (with case name and number) and any paper cases or documents for the court, the law clerk, the court reporter, and opposing counsel. Test courtroom technology in advance (arrange through chambers at 651-848-1180) and have a backup plan. The judge strongly encourages letting newer lawyers argue, especially motions they drafted, and draws no inference from the arguing lawyer’s experience level.

docs.t: Judge John F. Docherty (D. Minn.) — Status conferences and Rule 16 conferences
docs.x: Judge John F. Docherty, D. Minn.. docs.x: Judge John F. Docherty, D. Minn.. Settlement conferences: Comply fully with any Order for Settlement Conference. If there is any reason not to hold the conference (for example, a pending motion important to valuation or an outstanding critical deposition), contact chambers promptly.

docs.x: Judge Allison H. Goddard, S.D. Cal.. Mandatory settlement conferences: Complete discovery needed to evaluate settlement before the conference. At least 14 days before, counsel meet and confer in person or by phone (not email) on attendees, required approvals (such as a board), and insurance coverage and tenders. Lead trial counsel and the parties must attend; entities send someone with full authority, and insured parties bring a carrier representative with authority up to policy limits. docs.x: Judge Allison H. Goddard, S.D. Cal.. Sealing and protective orders: Sealing requests are scrutinized and need a specific showing; generic references to “competitive harm” will almost always be insufficient. Stipulated protective orders are filed as a joint motion with a Word copy emailed to chambers, and must include the judge’s sealing provision (court order required; serve the application on opposing counsel and any custodian, who must notify the ruling judge’s chambers of an intended opposition) and a sua sponte modification provision. A post-case disposition provision is recommended.

docs.t: Judge Allison H. Goddard (S.D. Cal.) — Communications, remote appearances, and settlement notice
docs.x: Judge Allison H. Goddard, S.D. Cal.. Communications, remote appearances, and settlement notice: Counsel may email efile_goddard@casd.uscourts.gov, a privilege that can be revoked for excessive or inappropriate use; appearing attorneys may call only for scheduling matters. For remote hearings, appear as if in the courtroom, with no background noise, a clear connection, and courtroom attire. On settlement, promptly file a notice of settlement or motion to dismiss and contact chambers (619.557.6162) if a court date is imminent; the court sets a telephonic Settlement Disposition Conference until dismissal.

Written motions to modify bond are preferred over bond hearings; for urgent requests, call the deputy for a date. Present bond documents, with the release order, to the deputy before bringing them to chambers; material-witness bonds note the arraignment date and counsel’s initials at top right. Nebbia and surety hearings need at least 24 hours’ notice, with the bail package (title, appraisals, loan statements) to the deputy and the U.S. Attorney 24 hours ahead; out-of-state sureties may appear by phone with prior approval and a notary present. In Class A misdemeanor cases, file a sentencing summary chart or memorandum

docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Discovery disputes: deadlines and conference first (trap): No discovery motion may be filed until the court holds a pre-motion telephonic conference, absent leave; noncomplying motions are stricken. Meet and confer first under Civil Local Rule 26.1.a. Request an informal discovery conference by a joint call to the law clerk within thirty (30) days of the triggering event: completion of the deposition, or service of the initial written response (or its due date, if none), not the date of impasse. If directed, exchange informal letter briefs (max five pages, 14-point font, stating each issue, position, and authority; only necessary exhibits, ordinarily not meet-and-confer correspondence) and lodge them by email to efile_White@casd.uscourts.gov. Conferences are informal and off the record; if unresolved, the court sets a briefing schedule.

docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Deposition disputes: For privilege, court-ordered limits, or Rule 30(d) disputes, suspend and meet and confer; if unresolved, call chambers for an immediate ruling. If the judge is unavailable, mark the transcript and continue, then request an informal conference within fourteen (14) days of completion of the relevant transcript portion.

docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Excusal only for extraordinary circumstances (travel distance alone isn’t one): confer with opposing counsel, then file a joint motion or ex parte motion at least fourteen (14) days before the conference. Confidential ENE statements (max five pages; exhibits discouraged) are due by email at least seven days before, covering the case, liability and damages with authority, the opponent’s strengths and your own weaknesses, a specific current demand with the basis for each type of relief (or why not yet and when), and prior negotiations. docs.t: Judge Brian J. White (S.D. Cal.) — Case management, status, and settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Case management, status, and settlement conferences: The Rule 16(a) CMC follows the ENE if the case doesn’t settle. File a Joint Discovery Plan on CM/ECF seven days before, covering each Rule 26(f)(3) item plus parties still to be served or added, initial-disclosure status, limited early discovery for settlement evaluation, any excess interrogatories and why, expert issues, threshold summary judgment issues, protective-order timing, and ESI issues. The scheduling order sets an MSC; a status conference usually comes about one month before it, where counsel should address whether the MSC date still makes sense. Expect status conferences every 30–90 days; a voluntary settlement conference can be requested anytime by call or email.

docs.t: Judge Brian J. White (S.D. Cal.) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Continuances (trap): Any request to continue an ENE, MSC, or scheduling-order deadline must be in writing at least seven (7) calendar days before the affected date. For a joint request to move a settlement conference, jointly call chambers first to find a new date. Include the original date, prior requests, good cause, any opposition and why, effects on other dates, and a counsel declaration on diligence and why the deadlines can’t be met.

docs.t: Judge Brian J. White (S.D. Cal.) — Protective orders and sealing
docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Protective orders and sealing: File as a joint motion stating whether the parties adopted the district’s Model Protective Order (highly recommended); explain any deviation with a redline, and lodge a Word version with electronic signatures and a signature line for the judge. Required provisions: court modification in the interests of justice or public policy, and the judge’s sealing language (compelling reasons, court order required, narrowly tailored, ECF Manual § 2.j and Civil Local Rule 79.2, a redacted public version filed with the sealing request). For one-year continuing enforcement jurisdiction, include the judge’s “Continuing Jurisdiction” paragraph.

docs.x: Judge Brian J. White, S.D. Cal.. Counsel must file a Notice of Appearance before any appearance, including informal telephonic and settlement conferences.

Later requests must show excusable neglect. Do not call chambers to reschedule. docs.t: Judge Jill L. Burkhardt (S.D. Cal.) — Mandatory settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Jill L. Burkhardt, S.D. Cal.. Mandatory settlement conferences: At least 21 days before the MSC, the plaintiff serves a written proposal with a specific demand; the defendant responds in writing with a specific offer before the meet and confer. Do not file these; include them in the MSC statements. At least 14 days before, counsel meet and confer in person or by phone (not email) on attendees with full settlement authority, anyone whose approval is required (such as a board), and insurance coverage and tenders. MSC statements (max 10 pages excluding exhibits) are lodged by the deadline in the MSC order (generally 7–10 days before) and may be confidential. They list attendees (with email and phone for each if by video) and cover facts, claims and defenses, proceedings to date, undisputed and disputed facts, legal issues, itemized relief sought, and settlement history.

Lodge documents by email to efile_Burkhardt@casd.uscourts.gov (not on CM/ECF unless directed); that address is not for communicating with the court.

Every proposed order must include five required provisions or the motion will be denied: good-faith designation under Rule 26(c); the court’s destruction of confidential documents absent an ex parte motion within 10 calendar days after the case ends; court modification for good cause; no change to court or local rules; and the judge’s sealing language. Sealing: do not seek to seal entire documents unless the whole document qualifies; file a redacted public version and address the basis for each redaction. docs.t: Judge Jill L. Burkhardt (S.D. Cal.) — Ex parte motions
docs.x: Judge Jill L. Burkhardt, S.D. Cal.. Ex parte motions: Unopposed requests should be joint motions; ex parte motions are only for exigent circumstances when opposing counsel is unreachable or refuses to join. No regular ex parte days or hours. Opposition is ordinarily due by 5:00 p.m. the next court day; for more time, place a joint call (or, if not feasible, a call limited to the extension sought). No replies unless requested or authorized.

docs.t: Judge Jill L. Burkhardt (S.D. Cal.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge Jill L. Burkhardt, S.D. Cal.. Communications with chambers: Only counsel of record may call; leave the case name, number, and call-back information. Staff will not estimate ruling times, give legal advice, or discuss the merits. No letters, faxes, or emails unless authorized, and do not copy the court on counsel’s emails. If a settlement notice is filed less than 48 hours before a court proceeding such as an ENE or MSC, plaintiff’s counsel must also call chambers and leave a voicemail. The judge expects civility and punctuality under Civil Local Rule 2.1.

docs.t: Judge Lupe Rodriguez, Jr. (S.D. Cal.) — Protective orders and sealing
docs.x: Judge Lupe Rodriguez, Jr., S.D. Cal.. Protective orders and sealing: File as a joint motion stating whether the parties adopted the district’s Model Protective Order (highly recommended); explain any deviation and attach a redline. Every notice of motion must state: “This motion is made following the conference of counsel that took place [in person/via videoconference] on [date].” For discovery disputes, counsel in the same county must meet in person and counsel in different counties by video (supplementing Civil Local Rule 26.1(a)). Failure to participate meaningfully can draw sanctions; if the other side doesn’t respond to a request to confer for more than three business days, counsel may contact chambers. Prisoner pro se cases may confer by phone.

docs.t: Judge Michelle M. Pettit (S.D. Cal.) — Discovery motions and privilege logs
docs.x: Judge Michelle M. Pettit, S.D. Cal.. Discovery motions and privilege logs: If leave is granted, expect an expedited briefing schedule. Organize by dispute, not request number; include disputed transcript portions; no counsel correspondence unless it shows a breached agreement. Hearings are rare. Unless the discovery plan or an order says otherwise, privilege logs list for each document: date, Bates range, author, primary and secondary addressees and other recipients (each with relationship to client or author), type, client, attorneys, subject, basis for withholding, and attachments.

docs.x: Judge Mitchell D. Dembin, S.D. Cal.. A party opposing must file a Notice of Intent to Respond, with a declaration explaining why it didn’t join, within 5 business days. docs.x: Judge Mitchell D. Dembin, S.D. Cal.. Deposition disputes: Only privilege, a court-ordered limitation, or Rule 30(d) justify instructing a witness not to answer. Meet and confer first, then call chambers at (619) 446-3972; if the court can’t take it immediately, move on to other topics and the court will respond as soon as practicable, possibly ordering a joint motion.

docs.x: Judge Mitchell D. Dembin, S.D. Cal.. Initial disclosures are due before the ENE/CMC. ENE briefs are due at least 5 days before, by messenger or email to efile_dembin@casd.uscourts.gov (confidential or shared), with essential facts and elements, a specific current settlement demand (or why not and when one will be possible), and prior settlement efforts. Excusal requires good cause (travel distance alone isn’t enough), conferring with opposing counsel, a call to the law clerk at (619) 446-3972, and then an ex parte or joint motion as instructed. The court may convert an ENE to a telephonic conference. To continue an ENE or settlement conference, confer with opposing counsel and call the law clerk; absent compelling circumstances, request at least 7 days before. A motion follows as instructed and needs good cause.

docs.x: Judge Mitchell D. Dembin, S.D. Cal..
